title: Anthropic mathematician claims to prove Riemann hypothesis, most famous problem in all of math

sentences.t: Anthropic mathematician claims to prove Riemann hypothesis, most famous problem in all of math

Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge said Friday, working with Claude, he had discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, the 1859 prime-number problem carrying a $1 million Clay Mathematics Institute prize.
He posted the proof in Lean, a language that lets computers verify each argument, and says it also confirms the broader Generalized Riemann Hypothesis.
Experts quoted say a confirmed proof would transform number theory, though verification of the coding was still to be completed.

title: The AI Riemann hypothesis proof is almost certainly true, independent mathematicians attest

sentences.t: The AI Riemann hypothesis proof is almost certainly true, independent mathematicians attest
Independent researchers, including MIT's Andrew Sutherland, separately compiled Alpöge's Lean proof without issues.
Sutherland said the proof was rechecked by the Lean kernel using only the three standard axioms, and that the chance anything is fishy is approximately zero.
A final comparator run was still pending to rule out any hack or redefinition of the original hypothesis.

title: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a holy grail of math problems with the help of AI

sentences.t: Anthropic worker claims to have solved a holy grail of math problems with the help of AI
Alpöge announced the claimed Riemann proof in a four-page statement on his website, a day after Anthropic's record IPO, saying Claude far outpaced him near the finish line.
The proof was released as about 17 million lines of Lean code — more than 250,000 pages of argument — rather than as a conventional paper.
Hours after the announcement the Clay Mathematics Institute still listed the problem as unsolved, and its president said the journey to real understanding would be long.

title: Epic defends competitive practices, promises to give more access to AI agents

sentences.t: Epic defends competitive practices, promises to give more access to AI agents
Epic Systems, the largest maker of electronic health records, said it would make it easier for companies to use AI to read data stored in its platforms.

Epic executives, responding for the first time to a STAT investigation, defended the company against allegations it undercuts competition by selectively withholding data access from rival app developers.
Epic said it received about 75,000 inquiries last year from organizations seeking to tap its data systems, which hold records on more than 280 million Americans.

title: VIEW Nasdaq plunges 5% a day after Anthropic debut, but investors still believe in AI

sentences.t: VIEW Nasdaq plunges 5% a day after Anthropic debut, but investors still believe in AI
Tech stocks slumped Friday to a 10% weekly decline in the Nasdaq, the biggest since 2020; Nvidia fell 14% Friday after Reuters reported the SEC was probing its accounting, and Anthropic dropped 9%.

Commentators called it an AI repricing reflecting slowing data-center buildouts, reduced funding for AI projects, and slower tech earnings growth, exacerbated by the Nvidia crisis and the Democratic midterm win.
Several investors still said they believe in the AI trade long-term, arguing AI adoption will keep driving economic growth and productivity.

title: Nasdaq wipes out gains for the year as Anthropic IPO fails to quell AI nerves

sentences.t: Nasdaq wipes out gains for the year as Anthropic IPO fails to quell AI nerves

The Nasdaq fell 5.28% Friday and is now down more than 2% for the year, having shed roughly $8.7 trillion in market value since its October 6 record high; the S&P 500 fell 3.7% for a seventh straight losing day.
Anthropic shares dropped 8.5% Friday to $88.91, just above the $83 IPO price, and the VIX fear gauge surged 86% on the week.
Investors are demanding evidence of return on the hundreds of billions being spent on the AI buildout, much of it raised through debt and equity markets.

title: Your 401(k) is full of AI. How to deal with the volatility

sentences.t: Your 401(k) is full of AI. How to deal with the volatility
The S&P 500 shed $5.6 trillion in market value this week and closed down more than 10% from its early-October record, exposing a concentration problem inside millions of 401(k)s.
Apple is almost 8% of the S&P 500, Microsoft almost 6%, and Nvidia 5%; the top 10 stocks — eight of them tech — make up roughly 40% of the index's value.
Advisers quoted urge retirement savers to check what their index funds actually hold, diversify beyond the same tech giants, and not panic-sell.

title: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?

sentences.t: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?

Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in its IPO plus $26 billion in a private placement, vaulting it past $1 trillion in value, while CEO Dario Amodei pledged safety would not bend to business or political pressure.

Legal experts told NPR that commercial pressure to deliver shareholder returns could cloud safety decisions, such as delaying release of risky models; each of the seven co-founders now holds a stake worth more than $20 billion.
A November 2026 METR assessment found Anthropic's AI capabilities improving at about twice the previous rate, driven largely by AI tools assisting its own researchers.

title: California faces horrifying budget hole as Xavier Becerra gets grim warning: ‘Dangerous stage’

sentences.t: California faces horrifying budget hole as Xavier Becerra gets grim warning: ‘Dangerous stage’

California's nonpartisan legislative analyst warned Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra of a $2 billion shortfall next fiscal year, growing to at least $15 billion by 2028-29 and potentially $30 billion by 2030-31 in a worst case.

Analysts fear an AI bubble could burst the stock market that is propping up state finances through capital-gains tax revenue, saying the market has advanced to a dangerous stage with indicators at their highest except at the dot-com peak.
The analysts suggested $6 billion in cuts or budget solutions next year to build a $4 billion cushion.

title: Keto diets high in long-chain fats may lead to inflammation

sentences.t: Keto diets high in long-chain fats may lead to inflammation
A new Science Advances study in mouse and human tissue models linked long-chain saturated fatty acids — such as those in red meat and egg yolks — to an inflammatory immune response.
Unsaturated and medium-chain fatty acids had more anti-inflammatory characteristics, and the increase was mediated by mitochondrial stress signaling and immune-cell activation.
Senior author David Gius said the data could inform keto eaters to favor medium-chain and long-chain unsaturated fats and lower long-chain saturated fats.

title: Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months

sentences.t: Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months

In a Washington University School of Medicine trial of 42 adults with obesity, prediabetes and fatty liver, published in Cell Metabolism, the ketogenic group (4% carbs, 73% fat) cut liver fat by an average 67%, versus 45% for Mediterranean and low-fat groups, despite similar roughly 10% weight loss.
About 50% of the keto group no longer met prediabetes criteria, versus 29% Mediterranean and 7% low-fat, and blood fat and cholesterol did not increase in the keto group.
Researchers noted the trial was small and lasted only four to five months; longer studies are needed.

title: Enel agrees US solar deal, taking North America renewables to 13.5 GW

sentences.t: Enel agrees US solar deal, taking North America renewables to 13.5 GW
Italy's Enel agreed to acquire a portfolio of solar plants in South Carolina from private developer energyRe, bringing its North American installed renewable capacity to 13.5 GW including storage.
The portfolio is 317 MWdc with expected average annual production of more than 540 gigawatt-hours, and an estimated $30 million in additional annual EBITDA once operational.
Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to US regulatory approvals, and is expected to raise group net financial debt by about $255 million once the plants are completed.

title: Senate OKs bill to speed energy projects, make data centers pay their way

sentences.t: Senate OKs bill to speed energy projects, make data centers pay their way
The Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act 62-33, to speed federal environmental reviews for energy projects and make data centers pay their own grid costs.
The bill also bolsters clean energy sources like wind and solar and was described as the most significant permitting-reform legislation Congress has passed in years.
It faces an uncertain future in the House; supporters call it a win for manufacturing and infrastructure, critics including Sen.
Jeff Merkley said it weakens environmental protections and tribal sovereignty.

title: Tesla proposes $3.1 bln Texas polysilicon plant for solar manufacturing

sentences.t: Tesla proposes $3.1 bln Texas polysilicon plant for solar manufacturing
Tesla is planning a $3.1 billion solar-grade polysilicon plant in Nueces County, southern Texas, according to a tax-incentive application filed this week.

The plant would create a new domestic source of polysilicon, a material primarily produced by China, which Tesla called a transformative investment in US solar manufacturing and critical-materials independence.

It would begin operations in 2030 and employ 515 workers by 2032; Elon Musk's goal is 100 GW of US solar manufacturing capacity, alongside a previously revealed $10.1 billion Houston facility for ingots, wafers and cells.

title: Lutnick asked battery startup Pure Lithium to accept US takeover, documents and source say

sentences.t: Lutnick asked battery startup Pure Lithium to accept US takeover, documents and source say

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asked Pure Lithium in July to give Washington a 51% controlling stake in exchange for funds to build a manufacturing plant the company would not own or control, according to documents reviewed by Reuters.

Pure Lithium rejected the proposal, saying it would invite public scrutiny, risk future capital-raising and cripple its ability to raise capital or pursue an IPO; Commerce rejected its 9.9% counterproposal.

Pure Lithium has developed a lithium metal battery it says is far more efficient than traditional lithium-ion and can be built without graphite, nickel or cobalt — a potential major advancement for energy storage if mass-produced.
